chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Port Stanley and Guy Lombardo (second version)
summary: Summer at the Ontario resort, snapshots held by his first wife, trouble getting paid, and meeting Lombardo.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Then you went up to Canada.
Right; Fort Stanley.
Fort Stanley, Ontario.
That was a summer resort; wasn't it?
That was a summer resort.
That must have been a
fabulous thing.
It was a fabulous thing.
We stayed there the whole summer. That was beautiful.
There should be some
pictures from that too; I can't believe that there wouldn't be. Are there some snapshots or stuff like that?
I don't know.
I bet your first wife
probably has all that stuff.
I bet she's got it all.
You better get a hold of her and see if she has some snapshots. There's got to be stuff like that around.
He thought that she was getting a little senile because (inaudible)
Something happened on that Fort Stanley job too; didn't it? That's when you began running into all that bad luck; didn't you not get paid or something on one of those jobs?
Something did happen but I really can't remember exactly what it was. We did have a little problem the last couple of weeks getting our money, but it was a beautiful job though.
It was supposed to be, yeah.
What band--there was a white band up there, some fairly well known. It wasn't Guy Lombardo.
We met Guy Lombardo just about that same time, because Guy was from London, Ontario; he's from that same area. We played music with Guy in London, Ontario; that's his home. That's where we first
met--that was before he came over to Cleveland. Then his brother, one of his brothers, not Carmen, the other guy who played tenor, he had a band in Toronto.
